Rashi on Pesachim 57a:10:1.hebrew: ישמעאל בן פיאכי - כשר היה, אבל אנשי ביתו היו בעלי זרוע:
Rashi on Pesachim 57a:10:1.english: Yishmael ben Piakhi - He was worthy, but the members of his household were violent.

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:11:1.english: Three hundred calves - For he would support many priests in his house.

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:11:2.english: What came of him - What recompense was paid [to him]?

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:11:3.english: The king and the queen - The kings of the Hasmonean dynasty.

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:11:4.english: A kid is better - A kid is better for eating than a lamb.

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:1:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: נימא תלתא תנאי הוו? לא, תרי תנאי הוו - תנא קמא דרבי יוסי היינו ר' שמעון, ותנא קמא דרבי שמעון היינו רבי יוסי, ומאי "אף" — אקמייתא:
Rashi on Pesachim 57a:1:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: "Let us say that there are three tanna'im? No, there are two tanna'im" - The first tanna [cited before] Rabbi Yosei is Rabbi Shimon, and the first tanna [cited before] Rabbi Shimon is Rabbi Yosei; and what [is the meaning of] "even"? [It refers] to the first [vegetable].

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:1:2.hebrew: לימא תלתא תנאי הוו - תנא קמא דר' יוסי ללפת ולכרוב ולא לקפלוט, ותנא קמא דר' שמעון ללפת ולקפלוט ולא לכרוב, ורבי יוסי ור' שמעון כי הדדי סבירא להו, דללפת ולכרוב ולקפלוט:
Rashi on Pesachim 57a:1:2.english: Let us say there are three Tannaim - The first Tanna of Rabbi Yosei [holds that it applies] to turnip and to cabbage, but not to leek; and the first Tanna of Rabbi Shimon [holds that it applies] to turnip and to leek, but not to cabbage; and Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon hold alike, that [it applies] to turnip, and to cabbage, and to leek.

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:1:3.hebrew: לא - ת"ק דר' שמעון הוא ר' יוסי, ות"ק דר' יוסי הוא ר' שמעון. ומאי "אף" דקאמרי תרווייהו? אקמייתא דתנא קמא דידהו קיימי, דהיינו אלפת: דקאמר תנא קמא דרבי יוסי "ללפת ולכרוב", וקאמר ליה רבי יוסי "אף לקפלוט" — כמו ללפת, אבל לכרוב לא. ותנא קמא דרבי שמעון נמי הכי קאמר: "ללפת ולקפלוט" כרבי יוסי, וקאמר ליה רבי שמעון "אף לכרוב" — כמו ללפת, אבל לקפלוט לא, דהיינו כתנא קמא דר' יוסי:
Rashi on Pesachim 57a:1:3.english: No - The first Tanna [whose opinion precedes that] of Rabbi Shimon is Rabbi Yosei, and the first Tanna [whose opinion precedes that] of Rabbi Yosei is Rabbi Shimon. And what [does] "even" that both of them say [refer to]? They refer to the first [vegetable mentioned by] their [respective] first Tanna, which is turnip: for the first Tanna of Rabbi Yosei says [it applies] to turnip and to cabbage, and Rabbi Yosei says to him, "Even to leek" — just as to turnip, but not to cabbage. And the first Tanna of Rabbi Shimon also says thus: [it applies] to turnip and to leek, like Rabbi Yosei, and Rabbi Shimon says to him, "Even to cabbage" — just as to turnip, but not to leek, which is like the first Tanna of Rabbi Yosei.

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:2:1.english: Ben Bohayan - His father's name [was] Bohayan.

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:2:2.hebrew: כפליים במעושר - גרסי': אני אתן לכם כפליים שיש לכם עכשיו פיאה, אתן לכם חולין מתוקנין ומעושרין:
Rashi on Pesachim 57a:2:2.english: Twice [the amount] in tithed [produce] - We read [the text as]: I will give you twice [what] you now have [as] peah; I will give you ordinary [produce that is] prepared and tithed.

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:2:3.hebrew: אין נותנין פיאה לירק - משום דמפקע ליה ממעשר, דכתיב (דברים י״ד:כ״ט) "ובא הלוי כי אין לו חלק ונחלה עמך" — מי שאין לו נחלה עמך חייב לעשר, יצא פיאה שיש לו נחלה עמך, דהפקר נינהו. וכן בשביעית, דהפקר פטור ממעשר, דכתיב (שמות כ״ג:י״א) "ואכלו אביוני עמך ויתרם תאכל חית השדה" — מה חיה אוכלת ופטורה ממעשר, אף אביונים פטורין מן המעשר:
Rashi on Pesachim 57a:2:3.english: One does not give pe'ah for vegetables - Because he thereby exempts it from tithes, as it is written (Deuteronomy 14:29): "And the Levite shall come, for he has no portion or inheritance with you" — [this teaches that] whatever [produce] he has no inheritance in with you is obligated in tithes, excluding pe'ah, in which he does have an inheritance with you, for it is ownerless. And similarly in the Sabbatical year, for ownerless [produce] is exempt from tithes, as it is written (Exodus 23:11): "And the needy of your people shall eat, and what they leave the beasts of the field shall eat" — just as a beast eats and is exempt from tithes, so too the needy are exempt from tithes.

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:3:1.hebrew: למה ליה למימר להן לא מפני כו' - הא קא יהיב להן כפליים, ומיחזא חזו דלא עין צרה היא:
Rashi on Pesachim 57a:3:1.english: Why did he need to say to them, "Not because [I begrudge]," etc. - Behold, he is giving them double, and they can see that it is not stinginess.

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:3:2.hebrew: דלא נימרו דחויי מדחי לן - ולא יתן לנו כלום, דמה לו ליטול זו וליתן פי שנים? לפיכך הוצרך לפרש להן טעמא של דבר:
Rashi on Pesachim 57a:3:2.english: So that they will not say, "He is putting us off" - and will not give us anything, for why would he take this and give double? Therefore, he needed to explain to them the reason for the matter.

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:4:1.hebrew: עורות קדשים - עור עולה וחטאות ואשמות וקרבנות ציבור, שמתחלקין עורות קדשי הקדשים לכהנים, כדכתיב (ויקרא ז) עור העולה אשר הקריב, וילפינן בזבחים (דף קג:) מעולה כל עורות קדשי קדשים:
Rashi on Pesachim 57a:4:1.english: Hides of consecrated [offerings] - The hide of a burnt offering, sin offerings, guilt offerings, and communal offerings; for the hides of offerings of the most sacred order are distributed to the priests, as it is written (Leviticus 7[:8]), "the hide of the burnt offering that he offered," and we derive in Zevachim (103b) from the burnt offering [that this applies to] all hides of offerings of the most sacred order.

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:4:2.hebrew: ולערב - שכל יום היו מחלקין אותן לאנשי בית אב שעבדו היום, שהמשמר היה חלוק לששה בתי אבות לששה ימים. ומה שהגיע ליומן, הן מרובה הן מועט, הוא נוטל, אע"פ שיש יום שמרבים היחידים להביא ביום זה מחבירו:
Rashi on Pesachim 57a:4:2.english: And in the evening - For every day they would distribute them to the members of the family [of priests] that served that day, since the [priestly] watch was divided into six families for six days. And whatever fell to their day, whether much or little, [that family] would take, even though there is a day on which individuals bring more on that day than on another [day].

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:4:3.english: Men of might - For there were among the priests [those who were] stronger than their fellows.

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:4:4.hebrew: לערב שבת - דכולי משמרה תיהוי התם, ולא יניחו לבעלי זרועות ליטול בזרוע:
Rashi on Pesachim 57a:4:4.english: On Shabbat eve - For the entire [priestly] watch will be there, and they will not allow the men of force to take [the hides] by force.

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:5:1.english: The prominent ones of the priesthood - The leaders among them.

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:5:2.hebrew: עמדו בעלים - כל כהני משמרות יחד, והקדישום לבדק הבית:
Rashi on Pesachim 57a:5:2.english: The owners arose - All the priests of the watches together, and they consecrated them to the Temple upkeep.

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:6:1.hebrew: בהר הבית - רחבה פנויה חוץ לעזרה, ויש שם מעלות, כדאמרינן בפ"ק דיומא (דף טז.):
Rashi on Pesachim 57a:6:1.english: On the Temple Mount - [This is] an open plaza outside the [Temple] Courtyard, and there are stairs there, as we say in the first chapter of Yoma (16a).

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:7:1.hebrew: קורות - מחוברין. עוביו של אילן קרי קורה:
Rashi on Pesachim 57a:7:1.english: Beams [korot] - [They were still] attached [to the ground]. The thick part of a tree is called a korah [beam].

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:8:1.hebrew: בייתוס - כהן גדול היה, וכן כולן, [והיו להן עבדים חמסנין וחובטין את העם]:
Rashi on Pesachim 57a:8:1.english: Baitos - He was a High Priest, and likewise all of them, [and they had violent servants who would strike the people].

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:8:2.hebrew: אלתן - מקלותיהן, כמו לא באלה ולא ברומח במסכת שבת (דף סג.):
Rashi on Pesachim 57a:8:2.english: Their clubs - Their sticks, as [in]: "neither with a club nor with a spear," in tractate Shabbat (63a).

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:8:4.english: Pens - For they would write letters for evil [purposes].

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:8:5.hebrew: אמרכלים - אמר כולו, על פיו נחתך כל צורך הקדש:
Rashi on Pesachim 57a:8:5.english: Amarkalim [overseers] - [This means] "he says all" [amar kulo], [meaning that] by his word every need of the consecrated [Temple] property is decided.

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:9:1.english: Who defiled - As it is written (I Samuel 2:22): "that they lay with the women."

Rashi on Pesachim 57a:9:2.hebrew: כריך ידיה בשיראי - וחציצה פוסלת בקדשים, דבעינן "ולקח הכהן", שיקח בעצמו. ועוד, דבזיון הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 57a:9:2.english: He would wrap his hands in silk - And an interposition invalidates [the service] in [matters of] sacred offerings, for we require "and the priest shall take" — that he take [it] himself. And furthermore, because it is a disgrace [to the service].

Tosafot on Pesachim 57a:2:1.hebrew: אלא מפני שאמרו חכמים אין פיאה לירק - אם תאמר: מכל מקום ליפטר ממעשר מפני שהפקירם, והפקר פטור ממעשר! וי"ל: כב"ה, דאמרי במס' פאה [פ"ו מ"א]: אינו הפקר עד שיופקר לעניים ולעשירים כשמיטה; וילפינן (בירושלמי) משמיטה, דכתיב: "תשמטנה ונטשתה", מה ת"ל "ונטשתה"? יש לך נטישה אחרת שהיא כזו, ומה היא זו? הפקר לעניים ולעשירים. א"נ, אפילו בית שמאי — דילפי מפיאה וסברי דהפקר לעניים הפקר — (הכא מחייבי, משום דהפקר בטעות הוה); וטעמא מפרש התם, דכתיב בפיאה: "לעני ולגר", מה תלמוד לומר "תעזוב אותם"? יש לך עזיבה אחרת שהיא כזו, ומה היא זו? לעניים ולא לעשירים. ומיהו בפיאה גופיה כולי עלמא מודו דפטורה, כדדרשינן בספרי: "ובא הלוי כי אין לו חלק ונחלה עמך" — יצא זה, שיש לו ללוי חלק בהן, שאם הוא לוי עני נוטל פיאה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 57a:2:1.english: "Rather, because the Sages said: There is no pe'ah for vegetables" - If you ask: In any event, let [the vegetables] be exempt from tithe because he declared them ownerless, and ownerless property is exempt from tithe! One can answer [that this follows] Beit Hillel, who say in Tractate Pe'ah [6:1]: It is not [valid] ownerless property unless it is declared ownerless for [both] the poor and the rich, like [produce of] the Sabbatical year; and we derive (in the Jerusalem Talmud) from [the laws of] the Sabbatical year, as it is written (Exodus 23:11): "You shall release it and abandon it." Why does Scripture state "and abandon it"? [To teach that] you have another abandonment that is like this one; and what is it? Declaring [produce] ownerless for [both] the poor and the rich. Alternatively, even [according to] Beit Shammai — who derive [this] from pe'ah and hold that declaring [produce] ownerless for the poor [alone] is [valid] ownerless property — (here they obligate [it in tithes] because it was a declaration of ownerlessness made in error). And the reason [of Beit Shammai] is explained there, as it is written regarding pe'ah (Leviticus 19:10): "For the poor and for the stranger." Why does Scripture state "you shall leave them"? [To teach that] you have another leaving that is like this one; and what is it? For the poor and not for the rich. However, regarding pe'ah itself, everyone agrees that it is exempt [from tithes], as we expound in the Sifrei: "And the Levite shall come, because he has no portion or inheritance with you" (Deuteronomy 14:29) — this excludes [pe'ah], in which the Levite has a portion, for if he is a poor Levite, he takes pe'ah.

Tosafot on Pesachim 57a:9:1.hebrew: דכריך ידיה בשיראי - פירש בקונטרס: וחציצה פוסלת בקדשים, דכתיב "ולקח הכהן" — בעינן שתהא לקיחה בעצמו של כהן. וא"ת: והא גבי לולב לא אמרינן הכי בפרק לולב הגזול (סוכה דף ל'.), גבי "לא לינקוט אינש לולבא בסודרא", רבא אמר: לקיחה על ידי ד"א שמה לקיחה? ותירץ ר"י, דהתם מיירי באוחז הלולב על ידי סודר כעין צבת, כגון שכרך הלולב בסודר ואוחז בסודר, שהסודר מסייעו להחזיק, וכי האי גוונא לא הויא חציצה. וכן משמע בההיא שמעתא דבהכי מיירי, דהא קאמר התם: "לא ליהדוק אינש לוליבא בהושענא, דילמא נתרי טרפי והוי כחציצה"; רבא אמר: "מין במינו אינו חוצץ" — משמע דבשאינו מינו חוצץ. והיינו משום דההיא הוי כעין דשמעתין דכריך ידיה בשיראי, דכי האי גוונא שייכא חציצה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 57a:9:1.english: That he would wrap his hands in silk [shirai] - Rashi explained: And an interposition invalidates [the service] in [the case of] consecrated offerings, as it is written: "And the priest shall take" — we require that the taking be done by the priest himself. And if you say: But regarding lulav we do not say so, in the chapter [entitled] Lulav HaGazul (Sukkah 30a), regarding [the statement] "A person should not hold a lulav with a scarf," [where] Rava said: Taking by means of another thing is considered taking? And Rabbeinu Yitzchak answered that there it is referring to one who holds the lulav by means of a scarf like tongs — for example, where he wrapped the lulav in a scarf and holds onto the scarf, so that the scarf assists him in holding [it], and in such a case it is not an interposition. And so it is implied in that sugya that it is referring to such a case, for it says there: "A person should not bind the lulav [together] with the hoshana [willows], lest leaves fall off and it become an interposition"; Rava said: "One kind with its own kind does not interpose" — which implies that with a different kind it does interpose. And that is because that [case of fallen leaves] is similar to [the case in] our sugya, where he wrapped his hands in silk, for in such a case interposition applies.
